title: Mayar and Driesh, Glen Clova
listingBlurb: Two Munros from Glen Clova — big ridges, obvious shape, not a puzzle.
summary: Forecast says windy-with-a-chance-of-clag, so this is the sensible shout: big obvious ridge, less faff, still two Munros and enough suffering to feel earned.
parkingNote: Glenshee ski centre is the beauty here. Big obvious start, easy to find, and no pointless warm-up just locating the car park. Still check signs and don’t park like a knob.
anchorRefsIntro: Quick map checks for key points, kept compact.

qualityMeter.headline: Pretty decent shout when the weather’s being awkward
qualityMeter.verdict: Big open ridge, less nav faff than the trickier link-ups, still enough climb to make your legs complain.

whyThisRoute.title: Why pick this day?
whyThisRoute.body: This is the decent shout when the weather’s a bit rough but not bad enough to stay home. The shape is simple, the ridge logic is obvious, and you still come away feeling like you did a proper day rather than a token leg-stretcher.
whyThisRoute.supporting:
It suits the sort of forecast where you want something readable. If the cloud’s being annoying or the wind’s up, this gives you fewer chances to drift into needless bullshit than a more exploratory day would.

It’s also a clean answer for a late-ish start. Big car park, straightforward start, and no detective work just to get going.

whatDayFeelsLike.title: What it feels like
whatDayFeelsLike.body: A steady climb onto open ground, then a broad high day where the shape mostly makes sense in front of you. It’s not dramatic mountaineering, but it does feel like a proper hill day once you’re out on the ridge.
whatDayFeelsLike.supporting: In decent visibility it’s simple enough. In clag it gets flatter and more serious fast, but still less awkward than some bigger wandering plateau days.

whatToLookOutFor: Ridge wind and cross-gusts: this was picked because the line is obvious, but if it’s blowing hard it still batters your pace.
Spring shoulder-season mix: dry-ish lower path can turn to old snow and icy patches higher up, so don’t assume one setup works all day.
Clag on the broad tops: even on this readable day, visibility can flatten fast and make easy bearings feel vague.
Cornice leftovers and loaded edges in colder spells: give crest lines a wider berth if the snowpack looks uncertain.
Busy Glenshee parking on decent forecasts: early start helps, and not blocking access keeps everyone happy.

recommendationBlock.title: Route shape / day flow
lines: Start at Glenshee and get the steady climb underway without much mystery.
Gain open ground and work onto the broader ridge.
Continue the ridge logic across to Driesh.
Decide on the day whether it’s a quick regroup-and-return or a longer stop if the weather behaves.
Head back the same broad logic rather than inventing nonsense just because a map has contour lines.

spots.title: Before the weather decides for you
spots.description: If it’s one of those changeable days, stop early once you hit open ground and reassess before committing higher.

spots.title: Shelter on the lee side
spots.description: Any slight dip or lee side out of the worst wind beats trying to have lunch on the most exposed bit like a hero.

spots.title: After the second top
spots.description: Worth a pause once both Munros are done, if only to enjoy the fact the hard bit is mostly behind you.

lookoutGalleryIntro: Quick visual reads for this ridge day: what you might spot, and a few things worth clocking if the cloud behaves.

lookoutGallery.title: Cottongrass
lookoutGallery.caption: White tufts in peat. Usually means the ground’s softer than it first looks. Why today: Wet spring ground and lingering moisture keep the boggier bits honest.
lookoutGallery.attributionText: © Mike Pennington. Geograph Britain and Ireland, image ID 6548063; mirrored on Wikimedia Commons with photographer credit.

lookoutGallery.title: Red grouse
lookoutGallery.caption: Loud, territorial moorland gobshites hiding in the heather till they panic and explode out of it. Why today: Spring breeding season makes them more visible and much noisier.
lookoutGallery.attributionText: © Alastair Rae (London, UK). Uploaded from Flickr; reviewed on Wikimedia Commons.

lookoutGallery.title: Red deer
lookoutGallery.caption: Deer moving across open slopes or standing about judging your life choices. Why today: Broad open ground and lower disturbance make sightings realistic on quieter stretches.
lookoutGallery.attributionText: © Mehmet Karatay. Own work; uploaded to Wikimedia Commons.

lookoutGallery.title: Open Angus moorland
lookoutGallery.caption: Heather, blaeberry, peat, and big rolling ground doing its usual “looks simple, walks longer” trick. Why today: This route is really about the broad ridge feel more than dramatic rocky nonsense.
lookoutGallery.attributionText: Use approved local/reference landscape image with proper source credit.

lookoutGallery.title: Views into Glen Clova
lookoutGallery.caption: If the cloud lifts, this is where the day feels properly worth the drive. Why today: Broken forecast often means patchy windows rather than a full socked-in washout.

disclaimerSection.title: Warnings / honesty
disclaimerSection.body: This is a planning page, not a permission slip to switch your brain off. Broad ground, changing weather, and winter leftovers can still make this a proper hill day. Bring a map, use your head, and don’t act surprised if the nice readable ridge still turns spicy in clag and wind.
